column1: Pharmaceuticals is one of the most profitable industries in North America.
column2: 制药业是北美最赚钱的行业之一。

column1: But do the drugs industry’s sales and marketing strategies go too far?
column2: 但是，药品行业的销售和营销策略是否过于激进呢？

column1: A few months ago Kim Schaefer, sales representative of a major global pharmaceutical company, walked into a medical center in New York to bring information and free samples of her company’s latest products.
column2: 几个月前，一家大型跨国制药公司的销售代表金·舍费尔走进纽约的一家医疗中心，向那里的人介绍公司的最新产品，并送去免费样品。

column1: That day she was lucky - a doctor was available to see her.
column2: 那天她很幸运，有一位医生有空见她。

column1: ‘The last rep offered me a trip to Florida.
column2: 上一个销售代表提议让我去佛罗里达旅行。

column1: What do you have? ’ the physician asked.
column2: ‘你有什么？’医生问。

column1: He was only half joking.
column2: 他只是半开玩笑。

column1: What was on offer that day was a pair of tickets for a New York musical.
column2: 那天提供的是一对纽约音乐剧的门票。

column1: But on any given day, what Schaefer can offer is typical for today’s drugs rep - a car trunk full of promotional gifts and gadgets, a budget that could buy lunches and dinners for a small country, hundreds of free drug samples and the freedom to give a physician $200 to prescribe her new product to the next six patients who fit the drug’s profile.
column2: 不过，舍费尔平日能拿出的东西，在如今的医药代表中很常见：一后备厢的促销礼品和小玩意儿，一笔足够请一个小国的人吃午饭和晚饭的预算，数百份免费药品样品，她还有权给医生200美元，请对方给接下来六位符合用药条件的患者开她推销的新药。
column3: on any given day|在任何一个寻常的日子里
column11: free drug samples|免费药品样品
column16: fit the drug’s profile|符合这种药的用药条件

column1: And she also has a few $1,000 honoraria to offer in exchange for doctors’ attendance at her company’s next educational lecture.
column2: 此外，她还能提供几份酬金，每份1,000美元，请医生出席她公司下一场教育讲座。

column1: Selling pharmaceuticals is a daily exercise in ethical judgement.
column2: 销售药品需要每天作出道德判断。

column1: Salespeople like Schaefer walk the line between the common practice of buying a prospect’s time with a free meal, and bribing doctors to prescribe their drugs.
column2: 像舍费尔这样的销售人员，游走在两种做法的界线之间：一种是常见的做法，请潜在客户吃一顿饭，以换取对方的时间，另一种则是贿赂医生，让他们开自己推销的药。
column4: walk the line between|游走在两者的界线之间
column6: buying a prospect’s time|换取潜在客户的时间

column1: They work in an industry highly criticized for its sales and marketing practices, but find themselves in the middle of the age-old chicken-or-egg question – businesses won’t use strategies that don’t work, so are doctors to blame for the escalating extravagance of pharmaceutical marketing?
column2: 他们所在的行业因销售和营销手法备受批评，却又陷入了那个由来已久的“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的问题：企业不会采用无效的策略，那么，医药营销越来越铺张，医生该不该为此负责？
column5: sales and marketing practices|销售与营销手法

column1: Or is it the industry’s responsibility to decide the boundaries?
column2: 或者，决定这些界限的责任应该由行业本身来承担呢？

column1: The explosion in the sheer number of salespeople in the field – and the amount of funding used to promote their causes – forces close examination of the pressures, influences and relationships between drug reps and doctors.
column2: 这一行的销售人员数量猛增，投入推广活动的资金也大幅增加，这迫使人们仔细审视医药代表与医生之间的压力、影响和关系。
column4: sheer|adj. 用来强调数量之大

column1: Salespeople provide much-needed information and education to physicians.
column2: 销售人员向医生提供他们急需的信息和培训。

column1: In many cases the glossy brochures, article reprints and prescriptions they deliver are primary sources of drug education for healthcare givers.
column2: 在许多情况下，医药代表送来的光面宣传册、文章抽印本和处方，是医护人员了解药品知识的主要来源。
column3: In many cases|在许多情况下

column1: With the huge investment the industry has placed in face-to-face selling, salespeople have essentially become specialists in one drug or group of drugs – a tremendous advantage in getting the attention of busy doctors in need of quick information.
column2: 这个行业在面对面销售上投入巨大，销售人员实际上已成了某种或某一类药品的专家。忙碌的医生需要快速获取信息，这让医药代表在吸引他们的注意力时占有很大优势。
column11: getting the attention of|吸引……的注意
column13: quick information|可迅速获取的信息

column1: But the sales push rarely stops in the office.
column2: 但推销活动很少止于医生的诊室。

column1: The flashy brochures and pamphlets left by the sales reps are often followed up with meals at expensive restaurants, meetings in warm and sunny places, and an inundation of promotional gadgets.
column2: 医药代表留下花哨的产品手册和宣传册后，往往还会请医生到高档餐厅用餐、安排他们在温暖晴朗的地方开会，再送上大量促销小礼品。
column7: followed up with|随后接着安排

column1: Rarely do patients watch a doctor write with a pen that isn’t emblazoned with a drug’s name, or see a nurse use a tablet not bearing a pharmaceutical company’s logo.
column2: 病人很少看到医生用一支没有醒目药名的笔写字，也很少看到护士用一本没有制药公司标志的便笺簿。

column1: Millions of dollars are spent by pharmaceutical companies on promotional products like coffee mugs, shirts, umbrellas, and golf balls.
column2: 制药公司在促销品上花费数百万美元，例如咖啡杯、衬衫、雨伞和高尔夫球。

column1: Money well spent?
column2: 这笔钱花得值吗？

column1: It’s hard to tell.
column2: 很难判断。

column1: ‘I’ve been the recipient of golf balls from one company and I use them, but it doesn’t make me prescribe their medicine’, says one doctor.
column2: “我曾收到过某家公司的高尔夫球，我用过，但这并不让我为他们开药方，”一位医生说。

column1: ‘I tend to think I’m not influenced by what they give me.’
column2: 我倾向于认为自己不会受到他们给予的东西的影响。

column1: Free samples of new and expensive drugs might be the single most effective way of getting doctors and patients to become loyal to a product.
column2: 免费提供新型且价格昂贵的药品样品，可能是让医生和患者忠于某一产品的最有效方式。

column1: Salespeople hand out hundreds of dollars’ worth of samples each week- $7.2 billion worth of them in one year.
column2: 销售人员每周分发价值数百美元的样品，一年累计达72亿美元。

column1: Though few comprehensive studies have been conducted, one by the University of Washington investigated how drug sample availability affected what physicians prescribe.
column2: 尽管尚未有大量全面研究，华盛顿大学的一项研究探讨了药物样品的可用性如何影响医生的处方行为。

column1: A total of 131 doctors self-reported their prescribing patterns - the conclusion was that the availability of samples led them to dispense and prescribe drugs that differed from their preferred drug choice.
column2: 共有131名医生自行报告了各自的处方习惯。研究得出的结论是，有样品可用，使医生配发和开具的药物与他们原本首选的药物不同。

column1: The bottom line is that pharmaceutical companies as a whole invest more in marketing than they do in research and development.
column2: 归根结底，制药公司总体上在营销方面的投资比研发投入更多。

column1: And patients are the ones who pay-in the form of sky-rocketing prescription prices - for every pen that’s handed out, every free theatre ticket, and every steak dinner eaten.
column2: 而患者则承担着处方药价格飞涨的代价——每支派发的笔、每张免费电影票和每一顿牛排晚餐，都伴随着高昂的费用。

column1: In the end the fact remains that pharmaceutical companies have every right to make a profit and will continue to find new ways to increase sales.
column2: 最终，制药公司完全有权利获得利润，并将持续寻找新的方式来提升销售额。

column1: But as the medical world continues to grapple with what’s acceptable and what’s not, it is clear that companies must continue to be heavily scrutinized for their sales and marketing strategies.
column2: 不过，医学界仍在努力厘清哪些做法可以接受、哪些不能接受。有一点很清楚：制药公司的销售与营销策略必须继续受到严格审视。
column4: grapple with|努力应对；设法解决
